My company went hybrid in January. Here is what the first six months looked like.

The productivity argument turned out to be a wash. Ticket throughput stayed flat. What changed was who did well. Two of our quietest engineers became noticeably more vocal in written discussions. One of our strongest collaborators started slipping through the cracks until his manager moved their one-on-ones to office days.

The real cost was onboarding. The three people we hired in the spring took longer to ramp up than earlier hires, and all three said the same thing: they didn't know who to ask small questions. We now give every new hire a designated question-answerer for their first month. It's a cheap fix.

Would I go back to five days in the office? No. But hybrid isn't free. You trade commute hours for coordination work, and that work has to land on someone's calendar or it doesn't happen.
